mechanism: The worker budget callback returns deadline minus monotonic time after a durable control read. Pre-callback anchoring subtracted that read latency twice.
A resulting early HTTPX timeout could reach the collector before a watcher exception. The collector correctly treated that raw timeout as a provider failure.
Worker finalization may later observe the global deadline and persist OPERATION_TIMEOUT, while the already-written provider failure remains.
correction: Anchor the remaining budget after the callback returns, before final rate admission.
Track whether the local remaining budget selected the effective request timeout.
On HTTPX timeout preserve any known watcher exception. Only budget-limited timeouts trigger an authoritative error-path check.
If that check returns, preserve any newly reported watcher error and convert to existing OperationTimedOut only after the selected local cutoff has elapsed.
Keep shorter/no-budget provider timeouts and early unrelated transport timeouts as provider failures; do not let a new slow control read replace an earlier provider failure.
No new durable callback follows successful final admission. The rate gate, socket cancellation controls, collector and worker persistence code are unchanged.

source_review: After-callback budget anchoring agrees with workers.tasks.remaining_seconds, which calculates remaining time after durable control reads.
budget_limited_timeout is per-request and reset before refresh; it is selected after admission against the configured timeout. A true value implies a populated budget_deadline.
No new durable callback occurs between successful final admission and stream dispatch. Existing actual-time pacing and transport-phase cancellation checks remain intact.
On HTTPX timeout, recorded watcher errors take precedence. Only worker-budget-limited timeouts trigger the new authoritative check; the watcher is checked again afterward.

Fallback OperationTimedOut requires the selected local budget cutoff to have elapsed. Early active-budget timeouts and genuinely shorter/no-budget provider timeouts remain HTTPX failures when no authoritative local stop is raised.
Existing canonical OperationTimedOut/OperationCancelled/OperationControlUnavailable semantics are preserved; no new public exception type or API field is introduced.
Lever inherits the corrected request and _get behavior. Local stops leave adapter health unchecked, whereas retained HTTPX errors continue to set SOURCE_NETWORK_ERROR.
unit_review: The six added methods exercise callback latency, four HTTPX timeout subclasses, shorter and absent worker budgets, late provider-check reclassification, authoritative exception identity, and early timeout preservation.
The module-local clock and dormant watcher model a valid pre-poll race deterministically. Real HTTPX Client/MockTransport behavior and client closure are exercised.
